focus.jnote: The backdrop is still hostile, though oil gave back some overnight. President Trump rejected Iran's conditional offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and reportedly told aides he expects strikes to resume after November's midterms; WTI settled ~$92.60 Monday and Brent ~$105, both easing overnight as Saudi Arabia restored ~3.5M bbl/day through its East-West pipeline. The 10-year yield sits near ~5.24%, a 19-year high, after Iran-driven oil pressure and hawkish Fed repricing; markets price ~70% odds of an October hike. Gold sits near $4,150, a roughly 7-week low, after a ~4% Monday plunge as yields and the dollar firmed. Futures are modestly higher this morning on the oil retreat, but this is a live, open-ended war-plus-rate-shock tape heading into PCE and payrolls — not one a Sniper sells premium into.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX, OXY) stays the one group with a war bid as the rejected Hormuz deal and blockade risk keep crude elevated. But be honest: this is a two-sided war trade, not a clean Sniper — oil already eased several dollars overnight on the Saudi pipeline restart, and one de-escalation or supply headline gaps any bull put the wrong way. The scanner examined the full universe and boarded nothing here. Watch-only, not a table-pounder.

The scanner confirms it: zero bearish names cleared confirmation.
